core_obligations: Independence: the displayed monomials are linearly independent by the cited basis theorem (proof lines 1361-1363).

Set up the induction: for n at least 2, the layer Delta_n is spanned by words of length at most n in the generators, hence by Delta_{n-1} together with words of length exactly n (proof lines 1365-1383).

Reorder the words: using the commutation lemma and the centrality of alpha, beta and gamma, each word of length n differs from its rearranged version by an element of Delta_{n-1}, so the layer is spanned by the monomials of total degree exactly n together with the previous layer (proof lines 1384-1400).
Close the induction: combining with the induction hypothesis gives that the displayed monomials span Delta_n, hence form a basis together with independence (proof lines 1401-1404).
proof_roadmap: Take independence from the cited basis theorem, and organise the spanning claim as an induction on the filtration index (proof lines 1361-1383).
Use the commutation lemma and centrality to reorder words modulo the previous layer, and finish by induction (proof lines 1384-1404).
difficulty_reason: The theorem states that the monomials A^i B^j C^k alpha^r beta^s gamma^t of total degree at most n form a basis of the n-th layer of the filtration of the universal Askey-Wilson algebra (statement lines 1349-1358). Independence is cited from the paper's own basis theorem, and the proof then establishes spanning by induction: the layer is generated by words in the seven generators, and the commutation lemma together with centrality of alpha, beta and gamma allows each word to be reordered modulo the previous layer, so only monomials of total degree exactly n have to be added at each step (proof lines 1361-1404). The step that carries the content is the reordering modulo Delta_{n-1}, since it is what converts an arbitrary word into the required monomial shape; the induction itself is then routine. H2.
